headlines: HIALEAH POLICE WARN OF SCAMMERS POSING AS OFFICERS TO DEMAND CASH
BEWARE OF FAKE POLICE PHONE CALLS TARGETING HIALEAH RESIDENTS
HIALEAH RESIDENTS URGED TO HANG UP ON SUSPICIOUS POLICE CALLS
posts.article: The Hialeah Police Department is alerting the community after scammers posing as law enforcement officers began targeting local residents over the phone. Fraudsters are telling people that they have outstanding warrants, pending cases, or unpaid bonds, and they are demanding payments. Authorities note that these callers sometimes use actual officer names, real badge numbers, and spoofed caller ID details to deceive targets. Officials emphasize that police will never contact anyone by phone to demand money to avoid an arrest. Anyone receiving such a call should hang up immediately and report the incident to Hialeah police at 305-687-2525.

headlines: MIAMI-DADE ISSUES MOSQUITO ALERT AFTER LOCAL DENGUE CASES CONFIRMED
DRAIN STANDING WATER AS MIAMI FIGHTS FALL MOSQUITOES
WHY MIAMI-DADE TEAMS NEVER STOP TARGETING BREEDING SITES THIS FALL
posts.article:
Miami-Dade County remains under a mosquito-borne illness alert following confirmed local dengue transmissions this fall. Even as rain decreases and temperatures cool, local mosquito activity continues across the area.

In response, the Mosquito Control Division of the Department of Solid Waste Management is deploying truck spray treatments using Bti larvicide alongside adult mosquito spraying. County technicians monitor more than 350 traps every week, while partnering with the Florida Department of Health, the University of Florida, and Florida International University on viral tracking and testing.

Officials urge residents to empty standing water, as species such as Aedes aegypti require only one ounce of water to breed. Property inspections can be requested by calling 311.
